config.title: Portal

intro.title: Portal
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a modal dialog that renders outside the normal React component hierarchy using a portal. You will learn how to use React's createPortal API to render content into a different DOM element, such as a separate div in your HTML. The core concept is managing DOM nodes to handle overlays, tooltips, or modals that need to break out of parent CSS constraints. This involves React's built-in ReactDOM.createPortal method and basic JSX structure. By the end, you'll understand how to implement portals for better UI control in your applications.
intro.usecase: React Portals are essential for managing UI components that need to break out of their parent container's DOM hierarchy, particularly for elements that should appear visually above everything else. This pattern is commonly used in production applications for modal dialogs, tooltips, dropdown menus, and notification toasts that must overlay other content. For example, when you see a login modal pop up on a website or a dropdown menu that appears over other page elements, developers often implement these using Portals. This approach ensures proper z-index stacking and avoids CSS overflow issues while maintaining React's component structure and event bubbling.

objectives: Construct a React portal to render content outside the normal DOM hierarchy
Apply the createPortal API to mount components into a designated DOM element
Configure event bubbling behavior for components rendered through portals
Initialize and manage portal target elements within the component lifecycle
Integrate portal functionality with existing React component structures
Manipulate CSS styling to ensure proper visual placement of portal content
Render dynamic content through portals based on component state changes

steps.title: Import React, useState, and createPortal from react-dom
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from 'react', and import createPortal from 'react-dom/client'.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the names of the modules you need from their respective packages.
steps.seedCode: // Import React, useState, and createPortal here
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React APIs and portal function are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react', and createPortal is imported from 'react-dom/client'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty fragment (<></>) initially.
steps.hint: Define a function called App that returns JSX. For now, return an empty fragment using <> and </>.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: A functional component named App exists and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the component is named exactly 'App' and returns an empty fragment (<></>).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Please create a function named App that returns an empty fragment.

steps.title: Initialize state for modal visibility
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, add a useState hook to create a boolean state variable named 'isModalOpen' with an initial value of false.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The syntax is: const [stateVariable, setStateFunction] = useState(initialValue).
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state for a toggle
const [isOn, setIsOn] = useState(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now has a state variable 'isModalOpen' initialized to false, which will control when the portal modal should be displayed.
successCriteria: The App component contains a useState hook that declares a boolean state variable named 'isModalOpen' with an initial value of false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your useState syntax. Make sure you're declaring a boolean state variable named 'isModalOpen' with an initial value of false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization isn't quite right. Remember to use the useState hook to create a boolean state variable named 'isModalOpen' with an initial value of false.

steps.title: Create a handler to open the modal
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a function named openModal that sets the modal visibility state to true.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls the state setter function with the value true.
steps.expectedOutcome: The openModal function is defined and ready to be called to show the modal.
successCriteria: The openModal function is defined and calls the state setter with true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it's named openModal and sets the modal state to true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The openModal function is not defined correctly. It should update the modal visibility state to true.

steps.title: Create a handler to close the modal
steps.instruction: Define a function named closeModal inside your App component that sets the modal visibility state to false.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls the state setter function with false as the argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a closeModal function that updates the state to hide the modal when called.
successCriteria: A function named closeModal is defined that sets isModalOpen to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function is named closeModal and sets isModalOpen to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it closeModal and it sets the state to false.

steps.title: Add a button to trigger the modal
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, add a button element with the text 'Open Modal' and an onClick handler that calls the openModal function.
steps.hint: Place the button inside the div. Use the onClick prop and pass the openModal function reference.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component renders a button that, when clicked, will update the isModalOpen state to true.
successCriteria: A button element is added inside the div
The button has the text 'Open Modal'
The button's onClick handler is set to the openModal function
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your button has the correct text and onClick handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added a button with the text 'Open Modal' and an onClick handler calling openModal.

steps.title: Create a portal container element in the DOM
steps.instruction: In the public/index.html file, add a div element with the id 'portal-root' right before the closing </body> tag. This will serve as the target container for your portal.
steps.hint:
You need to edit the HTML file directly, not the React component. Look for the tag and add
just before .
steps.expectedOutcome: The HTML file now contains a div with id 'portal-root' that can be used as a target for React portals.
successCriteria: A div element with id='portal-root' exists in public/index.html, placed just before the closing </body> tag.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Create the portal modal component
steps.instruction: Create a separate functional component named Modal that returns JSX for a modal dialog. Place it above the App component.
steps.hint: Define a new component that returns a modal structure. You can use a div with a class or style to make it look like a modal.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Modal component is defined above App, returning JSX for a modal dialog.
successCriteria: A functional component named Modal is created and returns JSX for a modal dialog.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the Modal component returns JSX for a modal dialog.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Modal component is not defined correctly. Create a functional component named Modal that returns JSX for a modal dialog.

steps.title: Implement the portal using createPortal
steps.instruction: Inside the Modal component, use createPortal to render the modal JSX into the portal container element (document.getElementById('portal-root')).
steps.hint: Call createPortal with the modal JSX as the first argument and the DOM element as the second argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Modal component now uses createPortal to render its content into the portal-root element in the DOM.
successCriteria: Modal component returns createPortal with modal JSX and document.getElementById('portal-root') as arguments.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using createPortal with both arguments: the modal JSX and the DOM element.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're calling createPortal inside the Modal component with the correct arguments.

steps.title: Conditionally render the portal modal
steps.instruction: In the App component's return statement, conditionally render the Modal component when isModalOpen is true, and pass the closeModal function to the Modal as a prop.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator or logical AND (&&) to conditionally render the Modal component based on isModalOpen. Remember to pass the closeModal function as a prop to Modal.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Modal component will only render when isModalOpen is true, and the closeModal function will be available inside Modal to close the portal.
successCriteria: Modal component is conditionally rendered using isModalOpen state, and closeModal function is passed as a prop to Modal.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're both conditionally rendering Modal based on isModalOpen AND passing closeModal as a prop to Modal.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using isModalOpen to conditionally render Modal and passing closeModal as a prop. Review conditional rendering syntax in React.
